why: Persian distinguishes an informal second person (تو: «تلاش کن») from a formal one (شما: «تلاش کنید»).
This file records which one each section speaks, so drift fails a build instead of accumulating.
It does NOT decide the open question — see `undecided` below. Choosing the product's voice belongs
to somebody who speaks Persian; informal is common in Iranian fitness apps and formal is safer for
a coach-facing tool, and that is not a call a regex should make.

observed.note: Measured by tools/copy/register.mjs, not asserted. 339 strings, 12 informal, 15 formal.
observed.pattern: Onboarding and goal declaration speak informally to the athlete; everything else is formal. That reads as a deliberate choice and is left alone.

programme.question: The programme screen is read by the athlete but its system messages were written formally («تغییرات شما ذخیره نشد»). Either the empty state becomes formal, or the system messages become informal.

informalStrings: sessions.logger.errors.noSets — «حداقل یک ست را پر کن.»
sessions.logger.errors.loadNotPositive — «… برای وزن بدن خالی بگذار.»
sessions.question: Same question, and this is the screen where it matters most: an athlete logging sets reads informal validation errors and a formal sync-failure message on the same page.

howToResolve: Pick one register for each undecided section, change that value here, run `pnpm copy:register`,
and the checker will list exactly which strings now violate it. Five strings in total.
That is the whole task — it does not require reading all 339.
